claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game's combat and platforming as centered around a one-hit-kill mechanic where both the player and enemies die instantly from a single hit.

citations.review_text:
I love Mirrors Edge and I love Cyberpunk 2077. This game just disappointed me. The one shot gameplay loop would be fine if the movement wasn't so buggy and clunky.

The gameplay doesn't feel fluid for me. It's just repetitive, which I know is the point, but not a good repetitive. I love difficult games; Sekiro and Elden Ring for example. But Ghostrunner doesn't give me that same adrenaline or excitement from almost anything.

I will say, the music is absolutely a banger and graphics are well done. I wanted to like this game, but I don't have the patience or excitement from one shotting enemies and dodging bullets. Maybe I'm just trash idk lol.

The game is well made, good graphics great movement but its honestly too difficult its one shot everything enemies and you. I understand however that it may just be that im ass at it but still if your looking for something similar to cyberpunk 2077 like I was this is not the game.

Bought it for the cyberpunk theme, unfortunately had to put it down. This is one of those "keep dying until you get it" games that appeal to some people but not me. Being able to get one-shot isn't for me, but I'm sure the raised stakes make the game enjoyable if that's your thing. Maybe I'll try it later with Assist mode, but if you found about this game only because you like Cyberpunk 2077 or Deus Ex, be aware the game has a much higher skill floor than these two. So make sure you like Souls-type games too (which I don't).

Not surprising that there's a lot of "skill issue" put-down talk within the game's community.

Wow. Such an adrenaline rush. Great visuals and sound.  Fab game
One hit you die, one hit they die. Sounds frustrating but once it clicks you feel like an unstoppable cyber ninja god. The movement is SO smooth - wall running, dashing, slowing time mid-air to slice 3 guys before you land. The soundtrack goes so hard too.


Went down like 400 timeees but never got bored. Every death is your fault so you just go again instantly.

If you like fast games like Titanfall or Doom, just buy it!!!! 🔥 📛 👨‍🚒

This is basically a parkour game. Running around and jumping at the right time. The game is one hit kill for both you and the enemy and quite punishing. So I guess it depends if you like this kind of game but it is not for me.

This game feels like someone turned a cyberpunk music video into a reflex test and then handed you a sword. And somehow, it works.

The best part is the speed. You’re wall-running, sliding, dashing, dodging bullets, planning your next move in half a second, and dying because your brain politely arrived three rooms late. But the checkpoints are quick, so failure doesn’t feel like a punishment. It feels more like the game saying, “Nice try. Now do it cleaner.”

I really like how the combat is built around precision instead of health bars. One mistake and you’re done, but one perfect run through a room makes you feel like a futuristic ninja with very serious anger management issues. The parkour, the one-hit fights, the cyberpunk visuals, and the soundtrack all push you into that flow state where you stop thinking and just move.

It’s challenging, stylish, fast, and very satisfying when everything finally clicks. Not a relaxing game, unless your idea of relaxation is being humbled by neon walls and laser guns, but it’s a really good one.

So fast-paced it hurts, camera is extremely sensitive even when turned down, one hit K.O. = restart checkpoint, fall to your demise very easily = restart checkpoint.... Could not enjoy getting through mission 2. Not a game I can enjoy, maybe this is something for the more hardcore crowd? Good luck.

First impressions:

Superb controls in a fast-paced platformer where you kill just as fast as you die. Great ambiance. Very promising title overall, I'd love to dive in further in the future.

One of those games you should have researched or was too good to be true. :S

Gameplay looks awesome. ✔
Borderlands Zero Kind Ninja ✔
Sword - Slice and Dice ✔

/ Hidden Gameplay/ ☠︎︎

If you die you die.☠︎︎
One shot you die ☠︎︎
Still stuck on the tutorial ..... you guessed it bcs you die.  :_)

Beyond Elden Ring?  At least I got passed the tutorial in Elden ring xD

Skill issue or Enjoy dying issue. 

If you willing to grind movement,manoeuvring whilst dedicating ample time to dodge a bullet , then I would recommend

If you just want to play and enjoy the game without having to master movement and manoeuvring, or dying constantly after a 1 tap. Do not Recommend. 

Rating 1/10

If you like fast games like Titanfall or Doom, just buy it!!!! 🔥 📛 👨‍🚒
One of the best games ive played

I played this a ton on PS5 and I cant express how much I love this game, the second game is alright, but first game is absolutely amazing. Dying in this game isn't frustrating, it feels like moving closer to a clean run.

The graphics and cyber punk world looks incredible. But get ready to die a lot. You have 1 life only - and a single hit kills you and you have to start at the nearest checkpoint. And even that doesn't work. I had made much progress in the game yesterday - today I booted it to see my latest checkpoint was at 5 checkpoints ago. Now I had to spend hours to go through the same difficult platforming, and one hit enemies - nope, can't do it again, 

Sure, the game is fun when it goes right but those moments are rare. I personally can't spend hours trying the same level section again and again just to make a little progress in the game. Not for me.

You better like doing the same thing over and over and over again. One hit kills and quick restarts are integral parts of the game, so sometimes you'll do the same 20 seconds of gameplay ten times back to back until you get it right. I'm sure for some its satisfying, but I find it incredibly grating.

This game is built around dying repeatedly in quick succession and has charge based abiities that don't recharge on respawn, meaning that you only get to use your abilities once every couple dozen attempts. That really should tell you everything you need to know about the level of polish in the game design.

It's supposed to be a flow state kind of game but the flow is really bad.

Gameplay is not very fun. The rest of the game though? Gorgeous. I should be picking this up just for the soundtrack.
What I've played of the game just reminds me of the Always Sunny bit with the sword vs the gun. It takes you just as long to close the distance between you and the enemy, and every dude's got a deadshot level quickdraw.
For a game that's all about being fast, a good chunk of it is you being thrown out of the flow once you reach a "combat" section and die a dozen times in a die-and-repeat trial and error loop. Even then, you got to rely on your slow-mo bullet time just to be able to dodge enemy shots. 
Sadly that's not what I was expecting. I'm sure there's many that'll like it though.

At first it feels incredible - visuals, speed, atmosphere. But soon it becomes boring die-restart gameplay. The whole gameplay is just memorizing every step. You are not mastering the game, you are just playing pattern-learning simulator.
10/10 Design.
0/10 Fun.

Looks great. Sounds incredible but honestly couldn't even get past the first three guys after about a hundred attempts. Not sure why anyone would ever want to endure such a grind in the name of entertainment.

Want to love it but I just can't. Warning to those that were lured like me for the cool cyberninja theme: this game is the kind of game where you die and respawn over and over, until you memorize the pattern of the enemies and find the optimal path to avoid death until the next checkpoint. The tags of the game don't describe what it really is: It's more a "super meat guy" kind of game than action/fast-paced (actually, it feels pretty slow sometimes).

The game is not bad, but for me, the gameplay completely kills the vibe here.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that movement mechanics such as dashing, wall-running, and wall-clinging feel inconsistent, clunky, or floaty.

citations.review_text:
I love Mirrors Edge and I love Cyberpunk 2077. This game just disappointed me. The one shot gameplay loop would be fine if the movement wasn't so buggy and clunky.

The gameplay doesn't feel fluid for me. It's just repetitive, which I know is the point, but not a good repetitive. I love difficult games; Sekiro and Elden Ring for example. But Ghostrunner doesn't give me that same adrenaline or excitement from almost anything.

I will say, the music is absolutely a banger and graphics are well done. I wanted to like this game, but I don't have the patience or excitement from one shotting enemies and dodging bullets. Maybe I'm just trash idk lol.

The dash controls are unplayable because they're inconsistent. On the ground, they activate on button press. When in the air, they activates on RELEASE. I can't tell you how ♥♥♥♥♥ this is. The wall cling is also god awful and you snap cling to walls when you don't want to, which gets you killed.

Go play Sprawl instead, it's 1000x better than this and it was made by one guy.
really good so far, only issue is that movement can feel really floaty at times

Unfortunately this game not only has terrible performance but the movement is so clunky and unenjoyable. Everything in the game can instakill you, object geometry is a mess and your momentum is constantly being reset. What little I played was painfully unfun and not worth investing time or money into.

Whether or not you can enjoy this really boils down to if you can get over the janky trash tier controls. I want to like it, the vibe is cool, the music is good, the visuals are solid, combat seems halfway decent. I'm usually a big fan of fast paced twitchy "quake" like games, but the controls, maybe some of the worst I've ever played. Consistently dying because you are wall running and jump to the next wall and somehow fly over it and go off into the ether like some weightless bozo is a different thing entirely. After an hour of pretty much just fiddling with controls and sensitivity and janky abilities like "blink" I just cut my losses. If you can deal with the controls, could be a cool game, but if not you're pretty much doomed.

This game shows how far we've come with fast Pace "slash" esc. games.

I remember playing this Game's demo when it got released for like 6+ Hours. I've never played a game like this before back then but I was a broke teen who couldn't get a 30$+ game like nothing.

So. Playing it in 2025 is... Rough. 

It makes me appreciate games like Ultrakill so much more. My biggest issue being the "choppy" feeling movement. Wall riding and ESPECIALLY the dash just feel wrong. Its not satisfying and often confuses you. 

Really like the Grapple tho. Nice Velocity and speed buildup with slides as well.

Another Quality of life negative I have is the lack of detail to sound or markers. This cannot be excused as much because they HAD games like Mirrors Edge to take inspirations from. Sounds. Please. I want to know where enemies are and how their cool downs are without having to use the Xray module or looking at the minimap. 

Is this game worth 30$ in 2025? 
No.

5-10$? Maybe. But if you havent finished Ultrakill. Id spend the extra any day.

Ghostrunner 2 will be interesting to see.

Review after playing 90 minutes, so [u]please[/u] take that into consideration. I also need to let off some steam and am admittedly using this game as a bit of a punching bag, however this negative review is genuine. I'll try to make it constructive.

[b]Ghostrunner[/b]: a game set in a large panel factory the size of Aperture Science, where you play as a cyborg Faith Connors with dialogue that isn't even a little bit engaging.

I love games with cool movement. This is a game that [i]looks like[/i] it has cool movement. It's passable for the most part, but needs more work. I seem to magnetise to walls even if I am trying to fall straight down instead of to wallrun. Unless you're sliding down a sloped surface, momentum isn't much of a factor, which takes a lot of energy away from my desire to send me and my blade hurtling towards enemies. I'm sure this is done so players don't lose control of the character, but I [i]yearn[/i] to travel faster than I'm able to at this point and the abrupt stop after dashing is killing my flow. There are puzzle sections, for some reason, and the type of puzzle keeps changing, for some reason. These are so painfully out of place I was asking myself why I was even bothering to continue. I'm still walking around in a physical play area but now I can't dash or do anything relevant to the main gameplay loop. Why am I doing this? Why is this in the game? I can see the effort that has gone into the level design, but sadly it ends up being quite disappointing; the platforming [i]with[/i] combat feels unintuitive sometimes and the platforming [i]without[/i] combat is bulky and takes up far too much game time. I presume this is to give the dialogue enough space to actually play out, but frankly the story is not particularly engaging up to this point. 

The writing and voice acting leave much to be desired. I understand the robotic nature of the interactions between 74 and The Architect, but I don't think this is a fair reason to have the world-b…

Maybe I'll come back to this game and play it more, but this game is simply inconsistent in platforming/combat and the times where I felt like a bad ass playing it were very short lived and ALWAYS fell flat because of poor mechanics; I don't feel like this is a "git gud" game, but more of like a puzzle game where you have figure out how to kill the enemies in the best path that provides the least chance for RNG killing you. 

My first time playing this game I played for about 2 hours, which usually means for me I will continue playing the game. At times I really was having fun and at times I felt like a bad ass; then using the same moves and inputs, I suddenly am getting killed instantly, I'm missing platforms, I'm moving fast and sliding through obstacles to leap off the edge of one and not know where I'm supposed to go, etc.

It presents itself as very fluid and fast paced and at times both the combat and platforming can feel like that, but the mechanics simply don't work as well as I've seen in other parkour/fast paced games. Wall runs don't center you on the wall (making the next jump either too low or worse you are too high and start climbing on top of a wall you can't even stand on) and jumping between tight corridors often has you grabbing the wrong platform/wall; these very poorly designed mechanics make every fast paced run fall flat EVERY SINGLE TIME.

Combat also seems to be very inconsistent; the core gameplay is basically dying over and over again so you can learn from your mistakes or understand what you need to improve upon. Once you develop a rhythm and understand the placement of the enemies, you will naturally start following the same path to kill them all. Following the exact same path and using the exact same inputs will work like 85% of the time, the other 15% you will die and have no clue what it was that killed you; I have never played a game where the combat seems to be so inconsistent.

The platforming needs a lot of work despite older parko…

claims.claim: Reviewers note that progress is lost if you quit before finishing a level because checkpoints are not saved between play sessions.

citations.review_text: I  just started , I played 6-7  times and just I regret buying this game . I also purchased the version 2 and at this point I'm evaluating to ask for a refund .  The reason that I'm still playing the very beginning of the introduction again and again and again despite the fact that I have activated all the options to simplify the game  ( extra life, slow down , etc) .  IMHO the "tutorial" at the beginning in unclear and there isn't the necessary progression in the increment of  difficulty that is necessary to introduce new players into the mechanics of this game. That makes simply piss me off.  Moreover, it's simply hilarious that I was able to go over some obstacles easily *WITHOUT* the help options . To be clear there is the autosave that doesn't permit to save any progress , so while during the game you will start from the last checkpoint in case of error, if you don't complete the level and you restart the game , you have restart from the very beginning.  So , you fall ? Checkpoint. The game crash or you shut down the game or your PC. You have to restart from the intro. After 7 times I'm simply tired  to restart. The fact that the checkpoint are not saved is pure evil fro the developers, IMHO. And I love this kind of games. They should take example from Portal * the game from Valve) : the game is explained in a well planned progression , clearly but without reducing the fun and the same I can say about the progression of the difficulty of the obstacles. Just my 2 cents.
A save system that does not respect your time - it's a shame because the game is excellent otherwise

It was ok. Not great, for the following reasons.
Firstly, the level designs are good, but the mechanics become repetitive after only two levels. And its not made in a way where its skill based. The AI of the enemies is terrible. They aim, and fire, almost like when you walk in their zone, they just aim and fire after a few seconds at your direction, like some kinda turret. Thirdly, probably the thing I noticed the second I started playing the game. The sound design sucks. The music is good, don't get me wrong, cyberpunk is my favorite music genre, but the sound design generally sucks, like, it doesn't feel cool killing anything, and I know it should since I played lots of games like it. The game is solidly built. Visuals are solid and the cyberpunk atmosphere is compelling, nice soundtrack and controlling the character feels great.

However, I feel like the actual gameplay is too boring and repetitive for how often you are forced to repeat it. It's a platformer, mild puzzles, and a ton of praying that a stray bullet doesn't make you repeat yourself. Which it will. "But I play dark souls and love challenging games". I also have played a ton of dark souls and others in that spectrum, some of my favorite games. The pain / frustration experienced in this one however, feels very un-rewarding and monotonous. 

Your tools are limited, and a single bullet touching you, or a single missed jump means you need to restart from the last checkpoint. Mercifully, the checkpoints are quite generous, but being at the top of my friend leaderboard for the first couple of levels and STILL feeling unsatisfied in the outcome is telling.

The engineering behind the game is solid. The fun is not there for me, at least not at the cost of the repeated monotony.

maybe I just suck at this game, but I've never had a game make me want to destroy things so quickly and given me carpal tunnel after just an hour. story seems fine, and the game looks beautiful, but I just don't like these super meat boy like games, even if it's first person instead of side on.

It’s a good game, especially if you hate yourself- I can’t really say I would reccommend it unless you are fully dedicated to spending your money on something that will make your blood boil hotter than Satans chili and will test your patience more than a fussy toddler in a grocery store. I put the game down because I suck at games like this and I don’t particularly like the feeling of being repeatedly stabbed in the kidneys, then again my opinion may have been different if I used a controller as opposed to a keyboard - That way, I feel like is the definitive way to play this game. 

The graphics are beautiful and the gameplay is smooth, but ultimately, I don’t know if I can reccommend this game or not. It’s VERY dependent on if you are open to stressful gameplay that will push you to your limits.

This game looks good but it makes little sense under the hood. The playstyle and physics are rigid, movement feels more like a dynamic FPS than a fast-paced action platformer. Platforming in a FPS is not fun. Also the katana is in your face in a weird way exactly where you want to check you landing point.
The narrative/objectives gimmick of being radio-guided gets old really quick and does not alleviate the feeling of a repetitive adventure in an empty world.
Level layout is a little short-sighted, you hop from arena to arena, blindspot after blindspot.
Obstacles courses feel recycled and reskinned very often, difficulty is ramped up with rhythm patterns to avoid which is not exalting.

And as in so so many games, epic (annoying & telegraphed) music all the time, even when nothing is happening.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the narrative as forgettable or of poor quality, noting that the plot and characters do not stand out.

citations.review_text:
Ghostrunner is trying to do too many things - and failing. Nothing in this game reinforces itself, and what shines in this game is just completely hindered by a mountain of boring/frustrating nonsense.

[h3]Story[/h3]

This is the central thing I want to harp on. The story in this game is horrid, and it is incredibly forced. It is almost exclusively people talking. Exposition dumping from characters that you essentially never see the entire game. All for a boring plot of ‘the people are oppressed by the big bad’ with no nuance, substance, or interesting characters. Do you ever see this evil force? Not until the end of the game. Do you ever see the effects of their actions? Well you see that everyone’s cyberpunk and trying to kill you but that’s it. I found nothing about this compelling, and I just wanted characters to shut up the whole game. You can just turn off voice acting, but then you notice the levels are structured for you to pay attention to said yapping.

[h3]Gameplay[/h3]

There are three types of levels in this game. Battle arenas, platforming sections, and digital “”puzzle”” sections. Battle arenas are where this game shines. Running around, dodging bullets, wall running, grappling, super jumping, slowing down time, throwing ninja stars - it’s all really fun. Even when you get hit by something you can’t see (and die in one hit, as everything one shots you), it’s still fun to go through these battle arenas. The issue is everything in between. 

In between the battle arenas are platforming and digital puzzle sections. These sections are clearly meant to be downtime in between battle arenas to hit you with some story. The worst are the digital sections. It is almost insulting how these levels drag the game’s pacing to a glacial stop. They consist of (easy) puzzles and completely drawn out tutorials for new abilities. Abilities that you don’t even need, by the way. You’re having fun, killing robots - STOP time to solve a rotating pipes puzzle so we…

The combat and music are good. I'm not sure if its just me but the levels have nice colors but feel lifeless and reused. The characters and enemies feel so flat. I get they're robotic, but there are many games that do a 1000x better job of developing them with a similar concept. The Mara boss fight was just so lame too. The architect was such an obvious villain on top of that. There's also this just oh-so fun bug that if you kill an enemy and die at the same time if freezes your keys and you have to exit to menu and lose progress. Not a bad game, like 5/10 or 6/10, but with how competitive Steam is, just buy Sekiro on sale and you'll have a million times more enjoyment...

70%
+ Unique, challenging gameplay
+ Great theme
+ Nice development of skills/gameplay mechanics
- Poor story
- Some enemies can make combat annoying
- Boss battles are weak

YOU CANNOT SAVE THE GAME MID LEVEL

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game features a fast-paced movement and combat system involving wall-running, dashing, and one-hit deaths for both the player and enemies.

citations.review_text: So challenging and so frustrating at the same time, but exhilirating! Awesome visuals and soundtrack, gameplay is ridiculously hard. Split-second sequence and you'll die. A lot.

This is a fast-paced action game where you're basically a cyborg ninja parkouring around slashing enemies left and right and it is FUN. 

The gameplay is stellar. Levels are a mix of platforming, wall running, and parkouring through cyberpunk levels and enemy arenas where you have to put those traversal skills to use while also mowing down enemies left and right to move on. You and enemies die in one hit so combat is about zooming around the arena dodging attacks at a rapid pace. Even dying has helps with the pace since you can instantly move on from the death screen and back into the action. You also get some skills that open up your options in combat and give you a few tools you have to use while platforming. There are bosses to and their designs in both combat and aesthetics are great.

The music and art scream cyberpunk throughout with some mix of Asian aesthetics primarily in the cyber sections.

The narrative is about climbing the impossibly tall tower to get back to the big bad who took you out and now controls the tower. It works and there are some interesting developments along the way.

I played Ghostrunner years ago and got pretty far, but I never managed to finish it. When the game first came out, I pirated it and made it all the way to one of the first serious boss fights - HEL. That boss fight was so damn difficult for me that I eventually gave up.

Fast forward 4-5 years later, and I decided to give it another try.

And this time, I finally finished it.

And honestly - the game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awesome.

If you're looking for a fast-paced, one-shot-kill game where basically everything can kill you in one hit, this is it. Get hit once and you're dead. There's not much room for mistakes, but that's exactly what makes the gameplay so addictive.

Parkour, wall-running, fast movement, trick shots and all kinds of crazy stuff, combined with skills and upgrades - all while playing as a half-robot samurai/ninja whose only weapon is a sword.

And yeah, I died. A LOT.

Sometimes I'd die 20 times in the same place because I just couldn't figure it out. Other times I'd die in the dumbest way possible like a complete bot. 

But when everything clicks - running through enemies, doing parkour, dodging bullets and slicing everyone up without getting hit - the game feels incredibly satisfying.

The levels are well designed, the gameplay is fast and addictive, and the skill and upgrade system adds some nice depth.

Overall, I had a lot of fun with it and I'm really glad I finally finished it after all these years.

Definitely recommend it if you like fast-paced games, parkour, katana combat and challenging gameplay.

9/10 - would die 500 more times.

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight that checkpoint placement is frequent and reasonable, which helps mitigate the high death count.

citations.review_text: Man, I owned this game since it came out but never actually played it until a few weeks ago and I am upset I waited so long! I got 100% in the game in about 33 hours, with DLC included. This was a super cool hack and slash parkour game set in a cyberpunk city. I  enjoyed everything about it, the graphics, the music, the abilities, the challenging layouts. Although, I will say this was by no means an easy game, it was one of the more difficult games I've ever played or tried to 100%, I don't rage at games very often, but I found myself getting increasingly frustrated playing this game. It was a hard one, but it wasn't entirely unfair as the checkpoints you are given are very very reasonable. If it weren't for the well placed checkpoints I'd never have finished this game. 9/10. The DLC was also very short, but the gameplay was almost more fun than the base game, worth checking out.

Fun fast-action platformer. Fantastic soundtrack and really great visuals. Though, the environments are very gamey, feeling like many of the places you navigate are not very realistic or serve any purpose aside from being a videogame environment meant for you to beat.

The gameplay was not exactly my cup of tea, though. I get lore-wise that you're supposed to be so hyper-advanced that all of your deaths are basically just your character (Jack) calculating, and when you win is like the actual events-- but gameplay-wise it can get pretty annoying that no matter what, you die from one hit. Some areas got quite frustrating, taking me something like 50+ attempts to complete one level. At least there are frequent checkpoints.

The story had a really good premise, but was executed somewhat lukewarm. Had a really predictable twist towards the end, and overall felt pretty cheesy from the dialogue. Was expecting something more on the level of Mirror's Edge but still not a bad game at all for someone looking for some neon cyberpunk action.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features an assist mode that can slow down the pace to help players adjust to the difficulty and controls.

citations.review_text:
A gorgeous cyberpunk themed game, that has you jumping and running and slashing in a fast-paced parkour style!!!

The gameplay can be so addicting by the time I got comfortable with the controls, I often restarted checkponts like "Wait, I can do this much better in one go" for that sweet dopamine hit! I love the fact that you can switch around between different upgrades during missions for whatever reason you need. You want to explore? Or do some heavy damage if you struggle in a level? Be as stylish as you can? Just put the ones you want are you're good to go!

The story is your regular revenge plot, pretty straight forward, but the gameplay is truly where all the fun is, being elevated by an absolutely amazing synthwave soundtrack that makes each movement and encounter with enemies much more intense and satisfying.

The game is also very inclusive as it offers an assistance mode that slows down the pace a bit for those who want to have a little more laid-back playthrough or if you need some help to get the feel of the controls and difficulty as you start at the beginning. But once you get going, those training wheels quickly fall off as you want to go faster and faster!!!

I absolutely LOOOVE this game, but I wouldn't recommended it to someone who has trouble being one-shotted or is not a fan of fast-paced FPS games and remembering patterns coupled with reflex-timed mechanics. If you have no issues with those, I HIGHLY recommend it to get it and have fun! ❤ Off playing the DLC next! :)

If you are a masochist this game is for you.
Ghostrunner isn't one of those run and slash games, you have no health and a single hit can kill you. It's more of a puzzle game more than anything at least to me. The challenge is in navigating the best way to deal with the threats around you in the most reliable and efficient way possible. I have died literally thousands of times in this game but I will admit that they were on me for the most part.

Pros
Story is pretty cool and in my opinion is fresh when looking at other games.
Visuals are beautiful.
Gameplay is really smooth at least on PC.
Dying is less detrimental than it is inconvenient which helps with how much you will die.
There is an assist mode which can help people who are not as good with fast paced games.

Cons
Steep learning curve and not a good game for people who haven't played a lot of games before.
The final two bosses are lacking in substance compared to the first one.
Enemies sometimes blend into the background without one of the early buffs in the game.

Play this game NOW!

it's very unique in it's gameplay style like a child born from mirrors edge and katana zero. I enjoy the relativistic pace of combat and almost seamless restarts upon death, the abilities are balanced and fun to use and the upgrade system is novel, if occasionally obstructive (the upgrades are like puzzle pieces and you've got like this grid you put them in, I think it's cool but it's not for everyone)

my only complaint is that the base game bosses, outside of the first, feel a bit janky and the final boss is, quite frankly, extremely disappointing from a gameplay standpoint. 
still worth the money though, if you get it on sale it's a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ steal





also there's a twist ending

A hack and slash in which you fight and parkour your way through a cyber punk megastructure.

[hr][/hr]
The titular Ghostrunner is Jack, an android-human hybrid equipped with superhuman sword fighting and parkour skills who you take control of after he awakens. The game presents you with a series of linear levels acting as obstacle courses for you to traverse. These sometimes feature small puzzles to mix things up, but their main challenge is found in the numerous enemies strewn around them who attack Jack on sight, with one hit being enough to reset him to the last checkpoint. With this setup, trial and error is the game’s central motive, with you having to find a working path through them by familiarizing yourself with their layout and figuring out the optimal way of disposing of the enemies.

Your only weapon is a sword, necessitating swift movement and dodging to get close to your enemies before finishing them off oni one swift strike. Beyond simple running, Ghostrunner lets you slide, wall-run and shoot a grappling hook to travel along ziplines, catapult yourself towards spots or move platforms. Most importantly though, you can dash, allowing you to change your movement direction in instant while slowing time to a crawl, thus allowing you to dodge projectiles. There are also special abilities you get access to for a limited time, e.g. shuriken throwing, which are used in both combat and puzzles. All of this enables satisfying gameplay centered around smooth-flowing action which makes you feel like a badass.

As you progress through the game, you also unlock various upgrades to upgrade your abilities, sometimes merely tweaking some numbers and sometimes expanding your skill set, e.g. giving you the ability to reflect projectiles. These upgrades use a rather unique assignment system, which represents them as differently shaped blocks you need to fit into a size-limited and uneven grid in order to activate their effects, forcing you to prioritize.

citations.review_text:
yo dudes, i wanna give my honest opinion on a really good game.
DISCLAIMER: i orginally played this game on console and was able to complete it on PC much faster, so i have a higher playtime than whats seen (closer to 30-40 hours)

first, the good stuff!!
the gameplay is smooth and settings are customizable to the T
plenty of secrets and lore to find and immerse yourself in
a nice TRUCK load of cosmetics to gain from secrets or the extra two modes (kill run and wave)
and finally the story is simple but captivating, small team of characters that aren't complicated
wide Varity of enemies that prove to challenge your skills and creative problem solving
and overall really fun to run through and be a cyber (fake) ninja.

now my gripes.
they dropped the ball with the cosmetics. 
there is little extra content and you can finish this entire game (dlc included) in less than 5 hours, 100% the game in roughly 15-20 hours (based off skill level)
you have to have FRIENDS WHO OWN THE GAME in order for the leaderboard to work! there is no online leaderboard to compare times, just "you and your friends"
 yeah thanks, my friends cant get past level one and call me a "super human with god reflexes"
and most of all, WASTED POTENTIAL.

its an awesome game with BARELY any extra stuff, the dlc is mid (cosmetics, not project HEL) and that's all it is, you pay almost 10 bucks for 2 out of 6 cosmetic packs. and that's all it is. no extra challenges to EARN the cosmetics, you cough up cash to basically get something you'll never see or use again. which is an EXTREME waste. you play and master all of kill run? you get this awesome reward that the game gives you BECAUSE YOU SPENT TIME AND EFFORT TO EARN. wave mode? get to wave 20 and finish it strong to get an EVEN COOLER SET!

metal ox? winter pack? Halloween? neon? all of it is paid cosmetics, and that's all she wrote. no extra challenges, no extra content, nothing. so there's NO POINT, its simply just eye candy for a game you may NEVER PLAY…
